thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — we pulled in a new community model 'lumen-lite-7B' for an internal pilot. Before we run quant experiments / hosted benchmarks, can legal confirm any egress / commercial restrictions? :eyes:

nick: Thanks for the ping. Can you paste the model card or license snippet? Need to check for non-commercial, no-derivatives, or export-control clauses first.

maria: Pasting the relevant part from the repo: ```
License: Community Research License v1.0
Clause 4: Redistribution allowed for research and internal evaluation only; commercial deployment requires separate agreement.
Clause 9: No modifications that create a derivative model for sale.
```

karen: If it's internal eval only, we can still run quant+latency tests on Dedicated, but hosting a public API or offering it via hosted tier is a no-go until legal signs off. Also need to know if weights include third-party licensed components.

devon: From infra side — if legal permits only internal usage we should lock the model to Private/Dedicated and disable outbound weight sharing. We'll also add an egress ACL so we don't accidentally sync it to S3 buckets with public ACLs.

nick: License-bot flagged an export-control note on line 2. For this model we need to confirm training data provenance and whether it was trained on sensitive datasets. I'll loop in legal counsel if provenance is unclear.

maria: Provenance is sketchy — sourced from a community repo with contributors across regions. No clear data statement.

eva: Suggest we treat it as 'high friction' in the intake flow: block hosted, tag for legal review, run closed quant smoke tests only. I'll add a triage label in the intake sheet.

karen: Operational checklist I propose (short):
- block hosted/dedicated public endpoints
- run quantization on a private dev pool (no cached KV uploads)
- record eval prompts & samples for regression monitoring
- snapshot model artifacts into secured bucket (encrypted)
- await legal sign-off for any external routing

maria: Adding one more: can we run a quick eval suite for safety/toxicity before we invest dev cycles? 10-20 prompts to flag high-risk outputs.

nick: Agreed. Legal is OK with internal-only automated evals. If we see anything concerning, we stop. I'll start the sign-off thread and request contributor license info.

devon: I'll prepare a private test job for quantization (8-bit & 4-bit) and make sure autoscaler won't spill to org-shared pools. ETA: tomorrow morning.

maria: Thanks. I've updated the intake row: https://sheets.fake/redwood/model-intake (triage: legal-needed, infra: private-only, evals: safety-smoke). Will post updates here when legal responds. :thumbsup:
